title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
statement:
Given a binary tree, find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of two given nodes in the tree.

The lowest common ancestor is defined between two nodes p and q as the lowest node in T that has both p and q as descendants (where we allow a node to be a descendant of itself).
inputFormat:
Line 1: space-separated strings mapping the level-order traversal of the tree.
Line 2: two integers p and q.
outputFormat: A single integer: the value of the lowest common ancestor node.
constraints:
2 <= The number of nodes in the tree <= 10^5
-10^9 <= Node.val <= 10^9
All Node.val are unique.
p != q
p and q will exist in the tree.

examples.explanation: LCA of 5 and 1 is the root 3.
LCA of 5 and 4 is 5, since a node can be a descendant of itself.
